title: Puddle painting with watercolours
description: Make a puddle of water on your paper, drop in a colour, and watch it swim and spread. Puddle paintings make soft skies, seas and rainbows that no one can get wrong.

body.heading: Make your puddle
paragraphs: Put your paper on a tray. Brush clean water onto the paper until it is shiny all over, like a flat puddle. Now dip your brush in a colour and just touch it to the puddle. Watch: the colour swims out all by itself.
Touch in a second colour next to the first. Where the colours meet, they mix and make a new colour. Blue meeting yellow makes a soft green, right there on your paper.

body.heading: Let it dry, then look
paragraphs: Do not touch your painting while it dries. Wet paper tears easily, and the colours are still swimming. When it is dry, hold it up. Can you see a sky? A sea? A sunset?
If you like, draw on top with a crayon when it is fully dry: a boat on your sea, a bird in your sky, a house under your sunset. Your puddle did the hard part for you.

takeaway: Brush water on first, then drop in colours and watch them swim and mix — let it dry before you draw on top.
ageGuidance: Ages 3–7, with a grown-up helping with water and clean-up.
materials: Watercolour paints and a soft brush
Thick paper or a watercolour pad
supervision: A grown-up sets up the water and paints, stays nearby while the child paints, and helps carry the wet painting to dry.
safetyNotes: Use non-toxic children's watercolours only, and wash hands after painting.
Keep paint water away from drinks, and wipe up spills at once so nobody slips.
Lay the wet painting flat somewhere safe to dry, out of the way of pets and toddlers.
screenFreeExtension: Go outside after rain and look at real puddles: what colours can you see in them, and what is reflected in the water?
